
=================================================================
#44 Jeon (轉)  (647 January)
Arc: The Chunchu Era · place: surabol · tone: political thriller — countdown
Logline: The sixth night’s tea turns to insult, the cavern throws Bidam out, a white horse burns for a falling star, and Yushin’s father’s stone goes warm.
=================================================================
[0] ══ DAY: DAY 6 ══
[1] ¶ Night rain. Five days of grain behind the palace gate. Bidam’s officers want a dawn assault. Bidam wants the score finished properly. He wants Yushin to come out again.
[2] ¶ **Sixth night.** Yushin does not come to the pavilion. Bidam sends tea anyway — two cups poured, one left steaming.
[3] Bidam: …He is not coming today. / Very well. Courtesy held until the sixth night.
[4] ▼ FLASHBACK 610 The headband
    [4.0] ¶ The Hwarang hall, the new boy’s first day. Two seniors lean across his desk.
    [4.1] Senior Hwarang: So he isn’t even a real True Bone!
    [4.2] Bidam: Hey, enough! / What did any of you do to earn True Bone? / You were merely born into it.
    [4.3] ¶ He punches the nearer one before the other can answer, then the second for good measure. Then he wipes his knuckles on his own black headband.
    [4.4] Kim Yushin: Thank you.
    [4.5] Bidam: What is there to thank? / Take this headband. Keep it, and no one will trouble you.
[4] ▲ end flashback
[5] ¶ Near midnight Yushin comes to the pavilion after all. He does not touch the cup.
[6] Bidam: **You Gaya wretch…!** / You dare call yourself the sacred country’s saviour….
[7] Kim Yushin: Lord Bidam. / Fifteen years past, in the Harmony Council — who was it that stood up for Princess Dukman?
[8] Bidam: ……
[9] Kim Yushin: That young Hwarang said he would choose the cleverest of the three. / Where did that man go, Lord Bidam?
[10] Bidam: …That man lived back when the sacred country was still a country.
[11] Kim Yushin: But it is not I who raised a banner against the sacred country…!
[12] ══ DAY: DAY 7 ══
[13] ¶ Seven days in, nobody pours. Four days of grain. Last night’s two cups are still on the pavilion table, and one of them was never touched.
[14] ── SCENE: Not a Kim ──
[15] ¶ **Bidam** finds the cavern the way a man finds a rumor. Sword on the lip. Beads in the fist. The navy coat comes off because he has heard Yushin wash here, and a man who wants what Yushin has will copy the wash if he cannot copy the name.
[16] ¶ He walks into the steam with nothing on but water and one hundred and eight beads.
[17] ¶ The three sisters are already on the far rock. Narim looks at him the way an eldest looks at a door that opened wrong.
[18] ¶ The spring does not hide much. Heat hits him low. He recites. The beads do not help.
[19] (monologue) Bidam: I came to wash. The sutra does not cover this. I am standing in a door I cannot close.
[20] ¶ The beads stop mid-count. He stares. The waterline drops.
[21] Golhwa: Wrong door. He brought iron. And that.
[22] Narim: He is not a Kim. The steam already knows.
[23] Hyullé: …The mouth. Before the water takes the blade.
[24] ¶ They do not stay women.
[25] ¶ Golhwa goes first — fire unfolding into a tiger the size of the rock, ember pelt, steam off the fangs. Hyullé’s silk becomes a water-serpent, long as the bowl, cyan scales. Narim’s elder-shape thickens into a moss-bear, leaves in the fur, the hill’s weight on four feet.
[26] ¶ He recoils. The beads jump. The sword is a hard black line he cannot lift in time.
[27] ¶ They kick him toward the light — tiger-shoulder, serpent-coil, bear-shove. Three beasts, one refusal. The night has him again. The lake keeps Kims. It does not keep slogans.
[28] ══ DAY: DAY 8 ══
[29] ¶ On the eighth night a star falls toward **the Moon Palace** — bright enough that both camps look up. Bidam does not invent the omen. He only names it in a useful direction.
[30] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)): I have heard that where a star falls, blood will surely be shed. This is likely an omen that the woman sovereign will be defeated.❞
[31] Bidam: You heard it. / Heaven has already voted against a woman on the throne. / 女主不能善理 — and now the sky writes it in fire.
[32] ── SCENE: The Moon Palace ──
[33] ¶ The rebel shout shakes the ground. Inside the Moon Palace **Queen Sunduk** goes pale. **Yushin** asks for leave to speak — and for a kite, a torch, and enough lies to edit heaven.
[34] Kim Yushin: Your Majesty — do not fear a falling light. / If they can read a star, they can also unread one.
[35] ¶ He flies the kite from the palace dark: a burning scarecrow rising where the star had fallen, so the night sky seems to take its light back.
[36] Kim Yushin: Look up. / Heaven changed its mind — or we changed heaven’s handwriting. / Hwarang, with me.
[37] ── SCENE: The Stables ──
[38] ¶ The kite buys one night. A sky can only be argued with for so long, and by midnight both camps are already arguing about what they saw. While the drums are still asleep, **Yushin** goes down to the palace stables alone and leads out the white horse.
[39] ¶ **Hangyul** has carried him for eighteen years, since the charge at Nangbi Fortress, to every border the queen sent him to and a few he went to without asking. The groom, a boy of fourteen, works out what the rope in the marshal’s other hand is for before anyone says it, and starts to cry with his mouth shut.
[40] ▼ FLASHBACK 612 Hanbyul
    [40.0] ¶ Seventeen, drunk, and asleep in the saddle. His first horse, **Hanbyul**, does what any good horse does with a sleeping rider and takes him where he always goes. He wakes at the courtesan **Cheongwan**’s gate with her lantern already lifted and her face already glad.
    [40.1] Cheongwan: You came? / …They said you swore to your mother you’d never come again.
    [40.2] ¶ He had sworn it. The horse had not. He gets down, draws, and takes Hanbyul’s head off at the gate in one stroke, then walks home past the lantern without looking at it. The song Cheongwan made about that night outlives both of them.
[40] ▲ end flashback
[41] ── SCENE: The Scorched Ground ──
[42] ¶ The star came down past the west wall of the Moon Palace, where the ground is still scorched in a long smear. Yushin walks Hangyul there himself. **Chunchu** is already waiting with two priests, a bronze basin, and a face that has decided not to argue.
[43] King Muyeol: …There are other white horses. Three in the stable. / Does it have to be this one?
[44] Kim Yushin: They know over there. Everyone knows which horse I ride. / Offer someone else’s horse and it isn’t heaven that laughs. It’s Bidam.
[45] ¶ He takes the halter off with his own hands. Hangyul, who has been led to a great many strange places at night, puts his nose into Yushin’s chest and waits for the reason, as he always has.
[46] Kim Yushin: Eighteen years. / If it weren’t for you at Nangbi, I’d have ended there. / …I’m sorry. This time I’m the one who brought you.
[47] King Muyeol: Yushin. / …Want me to do it?
[48] Kim Yushin: No. / He’s mine.
[49] ¶ He does it the way the rite asks and faster than the rite asks, so the horse never quite finishes turning his head. White goes down into the scorched black. The priests begin the prayer, and Yushin, who has never once let another man finish a sentence for him, lets them.
[50] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Bidam’s rebellion, 647)): He slaughtered a white horse and offered it at the place where the star had fallen, and prayed: “In the way of Heaven, yang is firm and yin is yielding; in the way of men, the sovereign is honoured and the subject humble. Should this ever be reversed, there is great disorder.”❞
[51] ¶ Across the field, on the Radiance wall, **Bidam** watches the smoke of the offering go up and asks an officer what was burned. When he is told, he puts his beads away for the first time in eight days and goes down to the lines to stand beside his own horse, **Bisamun**, for a while, saying nothing to anybody.
[52] [battle]
[53] ¶ Afterwards the groom leads out a young grey, too green for a marshal, the only horse left in the royal stable that nobody has been afraid of all week.
[54] Kim Yushin: Name?
[55] ¶ The boy shakes his head. He is still crying.
[56] Kim Yushin: Hanseul. / …It’s easy to say. Stop crying and try it.
[57] ¶ It is the last horse he names. He rides **Hanseul** out on the tenth day, and across the Yellow Mountain fields thirteen years later, and never once lets a groom catch him brushing it longer than the others.
[58] ── SCENE: The Stone ──
[59] ¶ Near midnight, at his desk in the palace, Yushin feels something warm against his wrist. He has carried his father’s stone in his sleeve for thirty years. It has never once been warm.
[60] ¶ He sets it on the desk between the lamp and the grain tally. Chunchu came in to say there are three days of rice left and not to tell the kitchen. He looks at the stone the way he looks at a letter in a script he can’t read.
[61] King Muyeol: …It’s a rock. / Why is your rock warm?
[62] Kim Yushin: My father had it from a spring under the hill. It warmed when the hill wanted him. / It hasn’t since he died.
[63] King Muyeol: And you’re going. With a rebel on the wall and three days of rice. To ask a spring something.
[64] Kim Yushin: Bidam says I was never of Silla. / Six nights I let him say it. I want to know— / …whether I am.
[65] King Muyeol: You’re asking a rock.
[66] Kim Yushin: I’m asking him.
[67] ¶ Chunchu doesn’t argue. He has just watched this man kill his own horse for a sky. He pours out the last of the wine, drinks half, and leaves the other half for whoever comes back.
[68] ¶ Yushin puts the stone back in his sleeve. He will go down before light.
[69] ¶ **A warm stone, a spring under a hill, and a father who once got very lost on purpose. Who was Kim Seohyun…?**
